utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Arcadia' by name among the cities in its service area, alongside Sierra Madre and San Gabriel (both already confirmed this session).

generation_supplier.notes: Arcadia's own site references Clean Power Alliance on its 'Sustainable Arcadia' and 'Environmental Services' pages as one of several sustainability partners, but no page fetched this session states whether Arcadia is an enrolled CPA member city with CPA as the default generation supplier, or merely a program the city promotes to residents who opt in independently. Clean Power Alliance's own site lists 38 member communities but only names 19 in the content retrieved; Arcadia was not among the named ones. Left null rather than assumed either way — this is a case where evidence was insufficient in either direction, not a case of no evidence at all.

county.notes: Arcadia is a well-documented Los Angeles County city, immediately adjacent to Sierra Madre and San Gabriel (both already confirmed LA County cities this session).

permit_authority.value: City of Arcadia Development Services Department, Building Services

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for the Irvine, Fullerton, Sierra Madre, and San Gabriel records this session. sce.com returned a DNS-level failure to automated fetch; the URL is confirmed to exist under this exact title on SCE's own domain via search engine indexing.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Arcadia/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: SolarAPP+ Approval Document and approval number (uploaded with the EDGE Portal permit application)

required_documents.notes: The city's SolarAPP+ page references a separate 'SolarAPP+ Eligibility Checklist' for acceptable project types, not independently fetched this session.

value: Log into the City of Arcadia EDGE Portal
Under the Building section, select 'Request Inspection'
Locate the permit by number (format SOLR-23-XXXX) or search on-screen
Follow the prompts to schedule the inspection

value.notes: The City's own Solar App+ page explicitly describes 'an online application for an auto-issued permit' for SolarAPP+-eligible projects, i.e. same-day/instant issuance.

other_conditions: Main dwelling rooftop, permitted, residential structures only — no ballasted or ground-mounted systems eligible for SolarAPP+
Only licensed contractors may submit applications

eligibility_constraints.notes: No specific kW size cap is stated on the SolarAPP+ page for Arcadia.

permit_fees.notes: The page states 'a processing fee is charged by SolarAPP+ NREL' but no dollar amount is given.
